title: 史記·卷一百五~卷一百八 (Shiji, Siku Quanshu, vol. 37 of 44)
shelf_note: Fits: a volume of the Siku Quanshu manuscript copy of Sima Qian's Shiji with the Jijie, Suoyin and Zhengyi commentaries, on the zh-shiji shelf. Juan 105-108 (Bian Que/Cang Gong, Wu Wang Pi, Wei Qi/Wu An, Han Changru).
structure_note: 168 records, 166 with OCR, 160 translated (2 pages lack OCR, 8 lack English). The volume holds four juan and the folio numbers restart with each one, so some backsteps are real. 8 backsteps and 22 repeats out of only 28 pages with a captured printed number also suggest misread folio numerals. This is not a splice. The four sampled pages run in order: juan 105, 105, 106, 108.

ocr_errors.problem: Garbled page furniture sits at the head of the transcription.

tr_errors.source: 不及九分至二分或四分五分此太過
tr_errors.english: falling short of nine tenths of an inch, reaching only two tenths, or four or five tenths, this constitutes deficiency
tr_errors.problem: The source says 此太過, 'this is EXCESS'. The English says 'deficiency', the opposite, so the pulse doctrine reads backwards.

tr_errors.english: When the primary vessels govern the illness, there is harmony.
tr_errors.problem: This is a doubtful parse that makes a free-standing sentence out of a clause running into the next line.

tr_errors.english: reaching the hands
tr_errors.problem: 手關 is cut to 'hands'. The phrase runs on to the next page.

ocr_errors.image: 欽定四庫全書 margin label; no 全一 or 二 at the head
ocr_errors.problem: The garbled margin label is transcribed as text and as a page number.

tr_errors.english: the liver spirits are six boys and three girls
tr_errors.problem: The source means six spirits: three boys and three girls. The English doubles the boys.

tr_errors.source: 肺神十四童子七女子七
tr_errors.english: the lung spirits are fourteen boys and seven girls
tr_errors.problem: The source means fourteen spirits: seven boys and seven girls. The count is wrong.

tr_errors.english: Jade Maiden Mother of Radiant Cloud <note>original: "雲光玉女子母"</note>
tr_errors.problem: The note misquotes the source (雲 for 云).

other.note: Junk furniture is translated into the reader text: 'Complete in one <note>original: "全一"</note>', 'structural marker: "厂"', 'Two'.

ocr_errors.image: 欽定四庫全書 (margin label)
ocr_errors.problem: Garbled furniture at the foot. It is not translated.

tr_errors.english: In the following year, the first year of the Yuanguang era <note>134 BCE</note>
tr_errors.problem: 'First year' (元年) comes from the next page.

reader_summary: This is the Siku manuscript of Shiji juan 105-108 with the three commentaries. The text is the right one and the main narrative reads accurately. The medical juan (Cang Gong) is weaker: one pulse statement is reversed (excess rendered as deficiency), spirit counts are wrong, and junk from the margin label shows up as text. The narrative chapters can be trusted. Check the technical medical passages against the Chinese.
book_verdict: The narrative pages are accurate. In the medical chapter one pulse statement is inverted, which is serious, and two numbers are wrong. Show it with a caveat on the Cang Gong pages.

title: 史記·卷一百十八~卷一百二十二 (Shiji, Siku Quanshu, vol. 41 of 44)

structure_note: 175 records, 170 with OCR, 166 translated. Five juan in one volume, so folio numbers restart and backsteps (12) and repeats (28) are expected. Some are probably misread numerals. Page 59 is a juan title leaf (juan 119), in the right place.

reader_summary: This is the Siku manuscript of Shiji juan 118-122 (Huainan, Upright Officials, Confucian Scholars, Harsh Officials) with the commentaries. The transcription is of the right text and the narrative English is faithful. On the juan title leaf, a line that is not on the page is transcribed and then rendered as a scholarly gloss.
book_verdict: The narrative is accurate and readable. The one embarrassment is invented apparatus on a title leaf, made from garbled margin text.

reader_summary: This is the Siku manuscript of Shiji juan 23-24, the Treatises on Ritual and Music (drawing on Xunzi and the Yueji), with commentaries. The transcription is accurate. The English handles the dense ritual and music theory well. It misreads the Wu dance as King Wu once, and one note ends in an invented sentence.
book_verdict: Good on the theory of ritual and music. One invented line of apparatus from margin junk, plus a moderate misreading of 武 as King Wu.

title: 史記·卷一 (Shiji, Siku Quanshu, vol. 1 of 44)
shelf_note: Fits: a volume of the Siku Quanshu manuscript copy of Sima Qian's Shiji with the Jijie, Suoyin and Zhengyi commentaries, on the zh-shiji shelf. The volume holds the front matter (the Qianlong-era memorial of presentation, the full table of contents) and juan 1 (Basic Annals of the Five Emperors).
structure_note: 237 records, but only 222 with OCR and 217 translated (15 without OCR, perhaps blank or plate leaves). The front matter (memorial, table of contents) has its own folio numbering before juan 1 begins, which explains backsteps (5) and repeats (12). The title '卷一' undersells a volume that is mostly front matter.

ocr_errors.problem: 日 (sun) is transcribed as 曰 (say) throughout. The English reads 'sun' correctly.

reader_summary: This is the opening volume of the Siku Shiji: the editors' memorial of presentation, the full table of contents, and the Annals of the Five Emperors with commentaries. The transcription is of the right text with one recurring slip (曰 for 日), and the English is faithful, including the Hundun story quoted in the Zhengyi.
book_verdict: Sound and showable. The front matter and the Five Emperors pages read well. The OCR confuses 日 and 曰, but the English is not misled.
